learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the poignant aftermath of war, the pain of memory, and the human need to let go of material possessions to find mental peace.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Set in Holland during and after World War II. The narrator's mother, Mrs. S, gave her precious belongings to an acquaintance, Mrs. Dorling, to keep them safe from the war.

Years after the war, having lost her mother, the narrator goes to '46, Marconi Street' to retrieve her mother's belongings. On her first visit, Mrs. Dorling coldly refuses to recognize her or let her in.
The narrator tries again. This time, Mrs. Dorling's daughter lets her in. The narrator sees all her mother's beautiful antique plates, silver, and tablecloths scattered in a tasteless, musty room.

Seeing her mother's precious things arranged so poorly in a stranger's house breaks her heart. The objects suddenly lose their emotional value because they are disconnected from the past and her mother.
The narrator leaves the house without taking anything. She decides to forget 'The Address' because holding onto those objects would only bring back painful memories of a life that no longer exists.

fun_activity.title: 🏺 The Memory Object
fun_activity.instructions: Pick up an old item in your house (a watch, a cup, a photo). Imagine someone else using it carelessly. How would you feel? This is exactly why the narrator chose to leave her mother's things behind.

exam_tips: 📌 The title 'The Address' is highly significant—it was the only link to her past, which she ultimately decides to forget.
📌 Character sketch: Mrs. Dorling is materialistic, selfish, and ungrateful. She never intended to return the items.
📌 Quote to remember: 'The objects... lose their value when, severed from them, you see them again in strange surroundings.'
quick_recap: ⭐ War brings not just physical destruction, but deep emotional trauma and loss of identity.
⭐ The narrator realizes that living in the present is more important than clinging to the past.
⭐ Human memory is deeply attached to material objects, but those objects cannot bring back the dead.
